title: deferred-route-pruning-causes-intermittent-cross-tenant-dns-resolution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers reported short-lived but recurring incidents where DNS queries from one tenant resolved to IPs owned by another tenant. Incidents cluster around autoscaler-driven node rotations and kernel upgrades to the router agents.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Customer support escalated a Sev1 for tenant 'acme-fin' showing NXDOMAIN -> foreign-A record briefly after autoscaler events. Repro steps captured with packet captures and resolver logs. Opening ENG-142058 for triage.

2026-03-06 - Diego Martinez (triage): Confirmed cross-tenant A responses in pcap and kube-proxy logs. Not transient DNS poisoning; responses originate from our egress leaf nodes with IPs that belong to other tenant VRFs. Hypothesis: stale forwarding entries during VRF programming window after node rotation.

2026-03-07 - Network RT (investigation): Found race in control-plane route pruning: when a tenant workload is migrated off a compute node, we defer pruning of per-tenant routes for 90s to avoid flapping. During that window, new route programming on replacement node can install overlapping ECMP entries leading to simultaneous presence of old and new nexthops on different routers. Under high load the L2 forwarding table sometimes forwards traffic to the old nexthop that still has an active DNS responder for another tenant due to SNAT port reuse.

2026-03-09 - Root cause analysis: Two orthogonal issues: (1) deferred route pruning delay combined with non-idempotent route installs allows short-lived overlap across VRFs; (2) per-tenant DNS resolver cache at the egress agent is not invalidated on route changes so stale resolver entries map hostnames to IPs no longer owned by that tenant. Both are required to reproduce.

- Hotfix (PATCH): Immediately force route reconciliation on compute node add/remove events (bump controller to call full reconciliation instead of deltas) and add a synchronous per-tenant DNS cache invalidation hook on route-change events. This reduces window to <1s.

- Medium term: Make route installs idempotent and add strict ownership checks in the forwarding agent so a route will never accept traffic for a tenant unless ownership metadata matches. Also reduce deferred-prune timeout from 90s -> 5s behind a feature flag.
- Long term: Add e2e scenario to CI that simulates rapid autoscaler churn and validates resolver cache behavior and VRF invariants.

2026-03-11 - Dev notes: Implemented cache-invalidation hook and forced reconciliation in branch fix/eng-142058-route-prune. Unit tests added for cache invalidation; integration test harness updated with synthetic churn workload.

2026-03-12 - QA: Canary rollout started to 5% of dedicated fleet (region-us-west-2 dedicated-pool-03). No further cross-tenant DNS incidents in canary after 24h. Observability dashboards updated (grafana link below) to track 'vrf-overlap-events' and per-tenant DNS cache miss rate.

2026-03-13 - Customer comms: Notified affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA for full rollout. Provided temporary workaround: pin workloads to stable nodes and disable autoscaler during maintenance windows.
2026-03-14 - Ops: Preparing gradual rollout to remaining Dedicated pools after security review sign-off. Monitoring checks added to auto-rollback if vrf-overlap-events > 0 for 3 consecutive windows.
Follow-ups: Add a postmortem doc with timeline, signal improvements, and runbook updates (assigned to Maya Chen).
